01.event: He missed the study hall and asked Rabbi Asi what was said there
01.outcome: Rabbi Asi reports Rabbi Yohanan's ruling
01.summary: Rabbi Elazar did not go to the study hall one day. He met Rabbi Asi and asked what the Sages had said, and Rabbi Asi told him Rabbi Yohanan ruled like Rabbi Yosei.
01.missing: Any event beyond a setting and a question and answer; any change
01.reason: A setting followed by a question and answer about a ruling is not a story (Shabbat 147a line); no conflict, no change.

02.actor: Rabbi Zeira's neighbors and a gentile superintendent
02.event: The superintendent refused to rent them his domain for an eiruv
02.turn: They asked Rabbi Zeira whether they could rent from his wife
02.outcome: Rabbi Zeira cited Rabbi Hanina that a wife may make an eiruv without her husband's knowledge
02.summary: A gentile superintendent living near Rabbi Zeira refused to rent his domain to his neighbors. They came to Rabbi Zeira and asked if they could rent it from his wife, and he answered with a ruling in Rabbi Hanina's name that permitted it.
02.missing: What happened after the ruling (whether they rented from the wife)
02.reason: There is a real incident (the refusal) and a ruling, but nothing narrated changes after the ruling; it sits between one-event-then-ruling (not) and a minimal story, so borderline.

03.actor: A man whose betrothed died; Rav Nahman's circle
03.event: He came before the sages after his betrothed died
03.turn: They told him to bury her or pay the ketubah; Rav Hiyya objected citing a baraita
03.summary: Rav Nahman, Ulla and others were sitting when a man came whose betrothed had died. They told him to bury her or pay her ketubah, and Rav Hiyya bar Ami challenged them from a baraita.
03.missing: Any action or change after the ruling
03.reason: Coming before rabbis and being ruled on, followed by scholarly objection, is R-C0's limit: no other narrated action or change.

04.actor: Rabbi Elazar ben Tzadok's family (descendants of Sena'av)
04.event: The Ninth of Av fell on Shabbat and was postponed to Sunday, their family festival
04.turn: They fasted but did not complete the fast because it was their festival
04.outcome: The fast was broken off before evening
04.summary: Rabbi Elazar ben Tzadok recalls that once the Ninth of Av fell on Shabbat and was moved to Sunday, which was his family's festival. They fasted but did not complete the fast because of the festival. The Gemara cites it as a legal proof.
04.missing: Conflict, causality beyond the practice, any development
04.reason: A one-time event with several actions, but little change and cited as evidence of practice; between a bare report and a minimal story, so borderline.

05.event: Rav came to Damharya and issued a practical ruling
05.turn: Rav Hanan bar Rava says Rav was only adding a safeguard
05.summary: Rav Huna cites a precedent: Rav came to Damharya and ruled in line with Rav Huna's view. Rav Hanan bar Rava answers that Rav was just fencing in an unguarded valley.
05.missing: The incident itself is only alluded to; no narrated events or change
05.reason: A precedent only alluded to inside a scholarly dispute; what is told is a single ruling with no change, so R-C5 applies rather than R-C6.

06.actor: A man who fell into the Great Cistern (from the Mishnah)
06.event: He fell into a cistern and emerged after three days
06.summary: The Gemara recalls Rabbi Meir's Mishnah incident of a man who fell into the Great Cistern, and discusses the objection that one does not cite miracles and what was miraculous about it.
06.missing: The incident is only cited from the Mishnah; the passage is discussion of it
06.reason: This is the Gemara discussing a story told elsewhere (the Mishnah) and trying to make sense of it, which is legal discussion, not a story.

07.actor: A man; Rav Aha bar Huna; Rav Yosef
07.event: A man betrothed a woman with a myrtle branch in the marketplace
07.turn: Rav Aha bar Huna sent the question to Rav Yosef
07.outcome: Rav Yosef ruled: flog him and require a bill of divorce
07.summary: A man betrothed a woman with a myrtle branch in the marketplace. Rav Aha bar Huna sent the case to Rav Yosef, who replied to flog him and require a divorce.
07.missing: Any narrated action after the ruling (the flogging is only ordered)
07.reason: One event followed by a ruling whose outcome is only implied by an order; Jeff ruled this shape not a story (2026-10-25).

08.missing: Any event besides a case brought to Rabbi Ami and his ruling
08.reason: Coming before a rabbi and his ruling is the only event; R-C0's limit.

09.event: The Rabbis urged him to marry and have sons
09.turn: He deflected, saying his daughter's sons are his sons
09.outcome: The Gemara explains he had become impotent from Rav Huna's long lectures
09.summary: The Rabbis told Rav Sheshet to marry and have sons; he answered that his daughter's sons count as his. The Gemara explains he was only putting them off, since he had become impotent waiting through Rav Huna's discourses.
09.missing: Actions beyond speech; the impotence is supplied as the Gemara's explanation
09.reason: Mainly speech with mild tension, plus a real event (his impotence) given as background; borderline rather than not.

10.actor: A depositor; Rabbi Meyasha's family; Rabbi Ami
10.event: A man deposited seven pearls with Rabbi Meyasha, who died without instructions
10.turn: The parties came before Rabbi Ami
10.outcome: Rabbi Ami awarded the pearls to the depositor, knowing Meyasha was not wealthy and because of the distinguishing mark
10.summary: A man left seven pearls tied in a sheet with Rabbi Meyasha, who died without telling his household whose they were. The family and the man came to Rabbi Ami, who gave them to the claimant because Meyasha was not rich and the man gave an identifying sign.
10.reason: Several narrated actions (deposit, death without instruction, dispute) resolved by a ruling, like the July cow case; more than coming before a rabbi.

11.event: He found a lineage scroll in Jerusalem
11.summary: Shimon ben Azzai says he found a lineage scroll in Jerusalem, and lists what was written in it.
11.missing: Any development beyond the finding; the contents are reports
11.reason: A single act (finding a scroll) cited as evidence for its contents, with nothing following; a bare report.

12.actor: Rav and Rabba bar bar Hana
12.event: Rabba bar bar Hana gave Rav money to buy land for him
12.turn: Rav bought the land for himself
12.outcome: The Gemara justifies it: violent sellers would respect only Rav, and he feared losing it to another buyer
12.summary: Rabba bar bar Hana gave Rav money to buy a plot of land for him, but Rav bought it for himself. The Gemara asks how he could act deceitfully and explains the sellers were violent men who honored only Rav, and Rav feared someone else would buy it meanwhile.
12.reason: Two actions with a change and a conflict (the agent buys for himself); the justification is Gemara commentary but the incident is narrated.

13.missing: Any event; this is a boast followed by scholarly questioning
13.reason: Abaye's boast and a sage's challenge with Abaye's exegetical answer are ordinary rabbinic dialogue, not conflict in R-C2's sense.

14.event: He asked Rabbi Eliezer, then Rabbi Yehoshua, whose request to honor first
14.turn: He asks about a divorced mother; Rabbi Yehoshua sees from his tearful eyes he is a widow's son
14.summary: A widow's son asked Rabbi Eliezer whether to serve water first to his father or mother, and was told the father. He went to Rabbi Yehoshua, got the same answer, and then asked about a divorced mother; Rabbi Yehoshua noticed from his teary eyes that he was a widow's son and mocked the irrelevant question.
14.missing: Events beyond speaking and going from one rabbi to another
14.reason: Mainly speech, but with movement between rabbis and a sharp, sarcastic exchange that adds conflict; borderline under R-C2/R-C7 shape 1.

15.event: She seized a saddlebag full of coins for her sustenance
15.turn: The Sages tried to recover it
15.outcome: They lacked the power to take it from her
15.summary: Rav Dimi reported that Rabbi Shabbtai's daughter-in-law seized a saddlebag of coins for her support, and the Sages could not take it back from her.
15.missing: Detail; the incident is brief and cited as evidence
15.reason: Two events (seizure, failed recovery) with some change, but told in one line as a precedent; borderline.

16.event: Two deeds for the same field came before Rav Yosef
16.turn: He awarded the field to the dated deed; the other protested
16.outcome: The loser asks for a document to repossess elsewhere
16.summary: Two deeds to one field came before Rav Yosef, one dated the fifth of Nisan and one just Nisan. He gave the field to the specific date; the other claimant protested and asked for a writ to collect elsewhere.
16.missing: Narrated action beyond the court case and ruling
16.reason: A case before a rabbi and ruling, with a protesting litigant; the ruling awards the property and the dispute adds conflict, so between not and borderline, prefer borderline.

17.actor: Rav Huna and his son Rabba
17.event: Rav Huna tore silk garments in front of his son
17.turn: He did it to test whether Rabba would become angry
17.outcome: Not stated; the Gemara discusses the halakhic difficulties
17.summary: Rav Huna tore silk garments in front of his son Rabba to test whether he would get angry. The Gemara asks whether this caused a stumbling block and answers that he had waived his honor.
17.missing: The son's reaction and any outcome
17.reason: A real deliberate act with a purpose, but the outcome is not narrated and the rest is commentary; events with little change, borderline.

18.missing: Anything beyond a report that two rabbis conducted halitza with five judges
18.reason: A bare report of what rabbis did, cited for its practice, with nothing following.

19.missing: The incident is only alluded to as a ruling
19.reason: A one-line report that Rav Yehuda ruled in a case of branches, cited as evidence; no narrated event or change.

20.event: A man sold land to Rav Pappa to buy oxen
20.turn: In the end he did not need the money
20.outcome: Rav Pappa returned the land to him, beyond the letter of the law
20.summary: A man sold land to Rav Pappa because he needed money for oxen. When it turned out he no longer needed it, Rav Pappa gave him back his land, which the Gemara says went beyond the strict law.
20.reason: Several actions with a change (sale, changed need, return of the land); something happened and someone responded, so a story.
